kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the source facts.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the panels, the table, and the TI block only; the attack structure is a KYP design.

kypExtensions.summary: The two-axes reading protocol (the DOSE axis = potency, the EFFECT axis = efficacy; a competitive antagonist moves only the dose axis with the ceiling intact and is overcome by ↑ agonist, a noncompetitive antagonist moves only the effect axis and is never overcome; single molecule alone that plateaus lower = partial agonist with Independent potency; activity below zero requires a constitutively active receptor = inverse agonist) — KYP's synthesis of the three panels and the four table rows into one protocol.
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the panels, the table, and the TI block as separate blocks and never states the which-axis-moved invariant or the molecule-ownership test; the two-axes framing and the ceiling-first reading order are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + mechanism antagonist-axes-map + the registry visual's panels + pivots

kypExtensions.summary: The four KYP mnemonics (COMPETITIVE SLIDES RIGHT; NONCOMPETITIVE SINKS DOWN / FLUMAZENIL WRESTLES FOR THE SEAT; PHENOXYBENZAMINE WELDS IT SHUT / SAME SEAT, LOWER LADDER, FREE RUNG / THE GAP IS THE GUARDRAIL) — the page's own memory devices are TITE and the Warning line and are carried VERBATIM and attributed as the source's; the four codes are KYP's design.
kypExtensions.rationale: The only mnemonics printing on book 233 are the source's own TITE line ('TITE: Therapeutic Index = TD50 / ED50.', with TITE in red bold) and the 'Warning! These drugs are lethal!' flag on the low-TI list; the four ALL-CAPS codes are KYP's design and are attributed as such.
kypExtensions.location: mnemonics + rapidReview.m3 + the visual's TITE banner and chips band

kypExtensions.summary: The two-compound miniCase (a surmountable right-shift at GABA A named as competitive antagonist + a buprenorphine-like lower-plateau-alone compound at μ-receptors named as partial agonist) with four distractors, each failing exactly one hinge: the noncompetitive misread of the right shift (ignores intact ceiling + rescue), the noncompetitive read of the lone compound (ignores ownership), and the inverse-agonist vocabulary flips (require negative efficacy nobody showed).
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid prints the four rows side by side and never asks the learner to route two experiments through the axes-and-ownership tests; the vignette and the four distractors are KYP's design.

notes: Census: pdfimages — ZERO raster images on pdf 255 / book 233. The VLM confirm (scripts/usmle-pipeline/ph7-vlm-census.ts, adapted from ph1-vlm-census.ts) was attempted TWICE and failed both times with an auth error (401 'missing X-Token header'), so the census was completed from the text layer plus the PDF's own VECTOR layer (PyMuPDF get_drawings: 147 paths; path coordinates, dash patterns, and stroke colors cross-referenced against word positions in the same coordinate system) — an exact fallback, stronger than a VLM sketch. PANEL MAPPING (documented correction): the production spec assumed A = agonist alone / B = agonist + competitive antagonist / C = agonist + noncompetitive antagonist, but the vector layer confirms the PRINTED mapping is A = Agonist + COMPETITIVE antagonist (the panel's second curve is pink, right-shifted, reaching the SAME 100% ceiling, label 'Agonist + competitive antagonist' at the panel's top right, red right-arrow between the two EC50 markers labeled 'Reduced potency'), B = Agonist + NONCOMPETITIVE antagonist (orange curve at the SAME midpoint with a ~50% lower plateau, label 'Agonist + noncompetitive antagonist', red down-arrow from the 100% ceiling labeled 'Reduced efficacy', both half-max L-markers stacked at the same dose = potency No change), and C = PARTIAL AGONISTS (the plain Agonist curve plus TWO green partial-agonist curves with lower plateaus, two red down-arrows 'Reduced efficacy', two 'Partial agonist' labels, and 'Independent potency' — the two half-max markers straddling the agonist's). Every panel carries the plain black 'Agonist' reference curve (hence 'Agonist' x3 in the text layer) — there is NO agonist-alone panel; the note and the registry visual carry the PRINTED mapping. THE A/B/C LETTER CHIPS: white letters on teal circles inside each panel (vector circles + white letter glyphs; the C chip prints fused with panel C's second 'Partial agonist' label as 'Partial C / agonist' in the text layer — raw line 46), and table rows A/B/C carry their own teal circle chips at the row-label left edge while the Inverse agonist row prints WITHOUT a chip. THE INTERLEAVE (documented): the text layer streams the three panels' labels in mixed order — the three '100' ticks together, then panel labels interleaved ('Agonist' x3 at lines 16/24/26), the two 'Reduced efficacy' labels (panels B and C) print at lines 21-22 and 34-35 while panel A's 'Reduced potency' prints later at lines 41-42, and 'Independent potency' interleaves between the second and third 'Agonist dose' x-axis labels (lines 57-64); additionally each panel's rotated y-axis label prints as vector text-outlines OUTSIDE the text layer (not quotable), while the TI figure's rotated '% of patients responding' IS text. TI BLOCK QUIRKS: the TI = TD50/ED50 print is a stacked display fraction ('TD50 median toxic dose' over a bar over 'ED50 median effective dose', with the '=' between two stacked fractions); 'TITE' prints in red bold at the head of the source's own mnemonic line; the five low-TI drug names print with red initial capitals (warfarin, theophylline, digoxin, antiepileptic drugs, lithium) and the closing 'Warning! These drugs are lethal!' carries the same red-letter treatment — both carried VERBATIM and attributed as the source's own. Outputs are STAGED under .usmle-pipeline-cache/staging-ph7/ — nothing is written into content/ (chapters/pharmacology.json, content manifests, visual-inventory, and the visual registry are owned by the promotion step; the note's visualId 'receptor-binding-map' is therefore not yet in visuals/registry.tsx by design).
